title: fix(logs): keep initial lines when following a new log file
body:
Closes #150843

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing initial records when `openclaw logs --follow` switches to a different log file whose size exceeds the previous byte cursor.

## User Impact

Following logs preserves the new file's available tail and subsequent appends in plain and JSON output, within the existing tail limits. Unreadable-config recovery continues reading local files rather than unexpectedly requiring a working, authenticated Gateway.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bind the existing byte cursor to its file path and reread without that cursor when the path changes. The reread uses the already-selected local source during config recovery, preserving the intent of #164158. Journal recovery and failed-reread retry behavior remain covered. Same-path inode replacement is outside this fix.

The new regressions control the polling/retry delay boundary instead of using real timers. Existing command tests now reuse the same fixture rather than duplicating its transport and output setup.

Thanks to @zhangguiping-xydt for the report and original repair. No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

## Evidence

Built CLI with a real isolated, token-authenticated Gateway on Linux / Node 24.21.0. A process-scoped clock simulates daily rollover without changing the host clock. File A contains 14 bytes; file B contains 45 bytes before an additional record is appended.

| Record | Baseline plain / JSON | Repaired plain / JSON |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A record | once | once |
| B first record | missing | once |
| B second record | once | once |
| B appended record | once | once |

A separate built-CLI control used malformed configuration and no Gateway: all four records appeared once, and both source metadata records retained `localFallback: true`.

The registered-command negative control against the previous PR implementation passed its four existing rollover cases and failed the new unavailable-config case by printing only the old file's record. The repair passes all five.

The baseline used the original PR revision with only the file-cursor repair removed; the repaired build includes current main. No real midnight wait or system-clock change was needed.

- Focused command, rollover, interval, and shutdown tests: **31 passed across 4 files**, including after fixture consolidation (wrapper wall time 2.60 seconds).
- Targeted Oxfmt and Oxlint: passed.
- Built-CLI live-provider check with `openai/gpt-5.4-mini`: returned the requested `P150791_OK` response with no tools.
- No full local suite or typecheck; hosted CI owns those checks.
- CI identified missing isolation annotations and four retired mock-baseline entries after fixture consolidation. The isolation contracts are documented and the stale entries removed. The full mock-factory ratchet passes locally (9,676 grandfathered factories); the affected command tests also pass.

Production delta against the merge base: +24/-0 lines. Tests and fixtures: +319/-170 lines. Documentation: +1/-0 line. Test baseline: +0/-4 lines. The production growth tracks the file identity and retains the selected source; the test fixture is shared rather than duplicated.

**Merge danger:** Two-way door; reverting restores the previous behavior without data or configuration migration. Blast radius is CLI log following across different file paths, including local-config recovery; no protocol, schema, default, or channel-delivery changes.
